findings.source_passage: Silly Mansoul swallowed it without chewing, as if it had been a sprat in the mouth of a whale.
findings.why_it_matters: This is among the most culturally recognizable of all the Extracts, widely cited in criticism and anthologies; its absence removes a key signature quotation from the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Pilgrim's Progress entry verbatim.

findings.source_passage: Io! Paean! Io! sing. To the finny people's king. Not a mightier whale than this In the vast Atlantic is; Not a fatter fish than he, Flounders round the Polar Sea.
findings.source_locator: Charles Lamb's Triumph of the Whale entry, after Montgomery passage
findings.why_it_matters: Lamb's mock-heroic verse is critically noted as one of the most tonally distinctive extracts, establishing the chapter's range from the sublime to the satirical; its loss flattens the tonal spectrum.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Charles Lamb entry verbatim.

findings.source_passage: These things are reciprocal; the ball rebounds, only to bound forward again; for now in laying open the haunts of the whale, the whalemen seem to have indirectly hit upon new clews to that same mystic North-West Passage.
findings.source_locator: From 'Something' unpublished entry, near end of source
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most interpretively weighted extract in the chapter — the 'mystic North-West Passage' phrase is a critical touchstone for readings of the novel's metaphysical ambition and is widely cited in Melville scholarship.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore this entry verbatim; it is indispensable.

findings.source_passage: A tenth branch of the king's ordinary revenue... is the right to royal fish, which are whale and sturgeon. And these, when either thrown ashore or caught near the coast, are the property of the king.
findings.source_locator: Blackstone entry, after Edmund Burke entries
findings.why_it_matters: The Blackstone extract carries significant interpretive weight for legal and political readings of Moby-Dick and is cited in critical literature on the novel's engagement with sovereignty and property.

findings.source_passage: There go the ships; there is that Leviathan whom thou hast made to play therein.
findings.source_locator: Psalms entry, fourth extract in source
findings.why_it_matters: This Biblical extract from Psalms is one of the most recognized scriptural invocations of Leviathan and contributes to the chapter's theological architecture.

findings.source_passage: I built a cottage for Susan and myself and made a gateway in the form of a Gothic Arch, by setting up a whale's jaw bones.
findings.source_locator: Hawthorne's Twice Told Tales entry, near end of source
findings.why_it_matters: The Hawthorne entries carry strong authorial-intertextual significance given the Melville-Hawthorne relationship and are noted in biographical and critical scholarship.

findings.source_passage: The quantity of line withdrawn from the boats engaged in the capture of this one whale, amounted altogether to 10,440 yards or nearly six English miles.... Sometimes the whale shakes its tremendous tail in the air, which, cracking like a whip, resounds to the distance of three or four miles.
findings.source_locator: Scoresby entry, after Elizabeth Oakes Smith
findings.why_it_matters: Scoresby is one of the primary naturalist authorities cited throughout Moby-Dick; his absence from the Extracts weakens the chapter's scientific register.

findings.source_passage: Mast-head ahoy! Do you see that whale now? Ay ay, sir! A shoal of Sperm Whales! There she blows! There she breaches! Sing out! sing out every time! Ay Ay, sir! There she blows! there—there—thar she blows—bowes—bo-o-os!
findings.source_locator: J. Ross Browne entry, near end of source
findings.why_it_matters: The compressed dialogue strips the phonetic comedy of 'thar she blows—bowes—bo-o-os!' which is the distinctive signature of the passage and its most-quoted element.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full call-and-response dialogue including the phonetic rendering of the lookout's cry.

findings.source_passage: The whale is doubtless the largest animal in creation. If you should write a fable for little fishes, you would make them speak like great whales.
findings.source_locator: Goldsmith entries, after Rape of the Lock
findings.why_it_matters: The Goldsmith-to-Johnson quip is a well-known witticism that contributes to the chapter's tonal variety and is cited in studies of the chapter's rhetorical range.

findings.source_passage: And what thing soever besides cometh within the chaos of this monster's mouth, be it beast, boat, or stone, down it goes all incontinently that foul great swallow of his, and perisheth in the bottomless gulf of his paunch.
findings.source_locator: Holland's Plutarch's Morals entry, after Isaiah
findings.why_it_matters: This passage's archaic diction and grotesque vividness are prosodically distinctive and establish the early modern register that gives the Extracts their historical texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Holland's Plutarch's Morals entry verbatim.

summary: The draft retains roughly a third of the source extracts and loses three high-severity signatures (Pilgrim's Progress, Charles Lamb, and the 'mystic North-West Passage' unpublished fragment) along with seven medium-severity omissions, constituting a serious failure of signature preservation across this chapter.
